transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

How I feel about my body and weight is completely controlling how I see myself and how I function at school. I'm a teacher, and lately, this obsession has just taken over my entire life to the point where I feel like I can't even do my job properly anymore.
Do you currently experience any behaviors such as restricting your food intake, bingeing, or purging in an attempt to control your weight?

Yes, I do. Most nights I completely lose control and eat massive amounts of food, like a whole pizza and bags of chips, though I don't purge or throw up. Instead, I punish myself the next day by skipping breakfast and lunch and forcing myself to exercise until I'm completely lightheaded, which happens about four or five times a week.
Have you experienced a significant weight fluctuation, such as gaining or losing a substantial amount of weight, over the past few months?
I haven't noticed any major weight gain or loss, but I am constantly obsessing over the scale. If it goes up by even a single pound, I feel like a complete failure as a person and a teacher.

You mentioned you don't purge or throw up after bingeing, but you do engage in excessive exercise as a form of punishment, can you tell me more about what you mean by 'forcing myself to exercise until I'm completely lightheaded'?

After a huge night of eating, I'll skip breakfast and lunch the next day and force myself to go for runs or do intense workout videos at home. I constantly tell myself that I don't deserve to stop until I've "earned" back the calories I ate. Since I'm fasting at the same time, this intense physical strain leaves me feeling completely shaky, dizzy, and lightheaded.
Do you feel that your worth as a person is heavily tied to your weight and appearance, and that when you fail to meet your own expectations in this area, you feel a deep sense of guilt or shame?

Yes, absolutely. My entire self-worth is completely tied to my body and what the scale says, and if it goes up even a single pound, I feel like a complete failure as a person and a teacher. I carry so much deep shame after I binge, which is why I try to hide it and desperately overcompensate the next day.
Can you estimate how often you have these episodes of binge eating followed by excessive exercise as a means of compensation, and does this occur at least once a week for the past three months?

Yes, it definitely happens more than once a week—usually about four or five nights out of seven. This exhausting cycle of binging and then trying to make up for it has been going on for about four months now.
Can you describe any other compensatory behaviors you engage in besides excessive exercise, such as fasting or using laxatives, to counteract the calories consumed during binge eating episodes?

I don't use laxatives, but I do fast by completely skipping breakfast and lunch the next day to punish myself. That fasting, combined with the intense jogging and workout videos, is my main way of trying to make up for the binging.
Besides the excessive exercise and fasting, have you ever used any other methods like diuretics, laxatives, or enemas to try to compensate for the calories you consumed during binge eating episodes?

No, I have never used diuretics, laxatives, or enemas to try to control my weight. My only ways of trying to "earn back" the calories are strictly fasting by skipping breakfast and lunch, and forcing myself to overexercise until I'm completely shaky.

Can you clarify if your excessive exercise and fasting behaviors are intended to prevent weight gain or to punish yourself, and do you feel these behaviors are necessary to maintain a sense of control over your weight?

It is definitely a mix of both. I feel like I am punishing myself for losing control by skipping meals and forcing myself to exercise because I don't deserve to stop, but I am also desperately trying to prevent weight gain. Since my entire self-worth is tied to the scale, these behaviors feel like the only way I can regain any sense of control.

You've mentioned that you don't purge or throw up after bingeing, but can you confirm if you've ever engaged in any purging behaviors, such as self-induced vomiting, in the past, even if it's not a current behavior?
No, I have never forced myself to throw up or used any other purging behaviors in the past. My way of coping has always been strictly fasting and overexercising to make up for what I ate.
